issues.legal_issue: Sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act do not bar evidence on whether the parties actually agreed to contract on the terms stated in a written agreement.
The agreement for sale was not sham or bogus where the asserted purpose of deterring the vendor from selling the land was unsupported by the pleadings and evidence.

Purchasers of immovable property covered by a registered agreement for sale are deemed to have notice of that agreement and cannot qualify as bona fide purchasers without notice if they failed to search the registration records.

A plaintiff seeking specific performance need not separately seek cancellation of subsequent transfers when those transferees are not bona fide purchasers without notice and can be directed to join in the conveyance.
A statutory prohibition on transferring agricultural land to a non-agriculturist bars execution of the sale deed, not execution of the agreement for sale.
A court may direct the vendor and persons claiming through the vendor to apply for required government permission and make a specific-performance decree conditional on that permission being granted.
Where one of two joint plaintiffs is not interested in specific performance, the decree may be limited to the interested plaintiff’s undivided share.
